# cp_pipeline_idr_training

## Overview

This Galaxy workflow is designed for automated image analysis and nucleoli segmentation using [CellProfiler](https://cellprofiler.org/). It begins by retrieving biological image data directly from the [Image Data Resource (IDR)](https://idr.openmicroscopy.org/) using specific IDs, facilitating reproducible research by integrating public repository data into a standardized processing pipeline.

The core of the workflow involves multiple stages of object identification and image manipulation. It utilizes several `IdentifyPrimaryObjects` modules to segment biological structures, supported by feature enhancement, masking, and image math operations to refine the regions of interest. These steps transform raw intensity data into discrete biological objects suitable for quantitative analysis.

Once objects are identified, the pipeline performs comprehensive morphological and signal measurements, including granularity, texture, intensity, and size/shape metrics. It also assesses image quality and relates objects to one another to capture spatial relationships. The final results are compiled and exported as spreadsheets, providing a structured dataset for further statistical training or biological interpretation.

## Inputs and data preparation

_None listed._


To prepare for this workflow, ensure you have the relevant Image Data Resource (IDR) identifiers ready for the IDR Download tool, which typically retrieves image data in standard formats like TIFF or OME-TIFF. Since this pipeline utilizes CellProfiler modules to build a processing sequence, you should organize your input images into a dataset collection to ensure efficient batch processing across all segmentation and measurement steps. Refer to the README.md for comprehensive details on specific parameter settings and image channel requirements. For automated execution and testing, you can initialize a job configuration using `planemo workflow_job_init` to generate a `job.yml` file.

## How to run (Planemo)

### Local Galaxy (default engine)

```bash
planemo run Galaxy-Workflow-CP_pipeline_IDR_training.ga job.yml --download_outputs --output_directory . --output_json output.json
```

Optional: `--galaxy_root /path/to/galaxy` speeds up spinning up a local Galaxy.

### Docker Galaxy

Append e.g. `--engine docker_galaxy --ignore_dependency_problems` (requires Docker).

### External Galaxy (usegalaxy.org / EU / …)

```bash
planemo run Galaxy-Workflow-CP_pipeline_IDR_training.ga job.yml --engine external_galaxy --galaxy_url SERVER_URL --galaxy_user_key YOUR_API_KEY
```

Create a reusable profile: `planemo profile_create myprofile --galaxy_url ... --galaxy_user_key ... --engine external_galaxy` then `planemo run Galaxy-Workflow-CP_pipeline_IDR_training.ga job.yml --profile myprofile`.

### Job file

- Generate a template: `planemo workflow_job_init Galaxy-Workflow-CP_pipeline_IDR_training.ga -o job.yml`
- Lint: `planemo workflow_lint Galaxy-Workflow-CP_pipeline_IDR_training.ga`

See **[Running Galaxy workflows](https://planemo.readthedocs.io/en/master/running.html)** in the Planemo documentation.

## Invocation outputs

After a successful run with `--download_outputs`, files appear under your chosen `--output_directory`. `--output_json` records CWL-style metadata for outputs (paths, checksums).

On an external Galaxy, use `planemo invocation_download INVOCATION_ID --profile ...` to fetch outputs, or track progress with `planemo workflow_track INVOCATION_ID`.

Workflow steps marked as **workflow outputs** in the editor are listed under **Workflow outputs**; exact filenames depend on tools and Galaxy configuration.

## Files

- `Galaxy-Workflow-CP_pipeline_IDR_training.ga` — Galaxy workflow export (JSON)
